---
name: zsh-bare-equals-word-aborts-command
description: In this zsh, an unquoted word starting with = (e.g. `echo =====`) is command-path expansion and aborts the whole compound command with "===== not found"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

An unquoted token beginning with `=` in the Bash tool's zsh (`echo ====`, `echo =====RETRY`) is
expanded as `=cmd` → path lookup; when no such command exists zsh aborts the ENTIRE compound
command before running any of it, so every probe chained with `;` silently produces nothing.

**Why:** Cost three round-trips on a live lfg bug report (2026-09-07) because the separators were
the only thing wrong with otherwise-correct commands.

**How to apply:** Quote separators (`echo '====='`) or use `printf -- '-----\n'`; never start an
unquoted word with `=`. Related: [[probe-shape-before-scripting]].
EOF
